title: The steelman rule
summary: Learn to say the other side's best point before your own, then debate whether kids should choose their own bedtime.

steps.title: Steelman the other side
steps.body:
A steelman is the opposite of a strawman. A strawman is a weak, easy-to-knock-down version of the other side's argument, one nobody actually believes. A steelman is the strongest, most honest version of it, the best point the other side actually has.

Here is the rule: before you say your own point, say the other side's best point first, in your own words. Not a weak version of it, the real one, the one that would make a smart listener nod along.

This wins arguments for two reasons. First, it shows you actually listened, so people trust the rest of what you say more. Second, it forces you to understand the strongest case against you, which means your own answer has to be strong enough to actually beat it, not just louder.

The question of the week is: If you could change one rule at home, which one, and is that fair to everyone? Think about it before the debate, since steelmanning is exactly what you need in a minute: the rule you want to change probably exists for a reason, and that reason is the other side's best point.

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record part of the debate, or record yourself afterward steelmanning the other side's best point before giving your own.
